title: Stereotypes Vol. 005

description.main: A self-published zine in Lucien Samaha's ftA (from the Archive) series, collecting his Stereotypes collages built from vintage Arabic-language movie-magazine imagery.
description.extended:
A volume in the Lebanese-American artist Lucien Samaha's self-published ftA (from the Archive) series, Stereotypes Vol. 005 collects collages that splice the swaggering leading men and starlets of vintage Arabic-language movie magazines into pointed, funny recombinations.

Issued in New York in 2022 as a signed first-edition softcover, the zine draws on Samaha's collage practice rooted in his long engagement with Arab visual culture — he was an early member of the Arab Image Foundation, and his cut-and-paste works recirculate the printed ephemera of mid-century Beirut and Cairo pop cinema, probing the stock characters its title names.

Samaha (b. Beirut) is best known as a pioneer of digital photography — while at Kodak he shot among the first digital photographs ever taken — and as an obsessive archivist of his own life: three decades of images from airline galleys, New York nightclubs, and the Windows on the World DJ booth, sequenced into ongoing self-published series like FLM and ftA.

notes: Series: ftA (from the Archive), no. 005. No ISBN (self-published). Sold as signed first edition at Dashwood Books.
